title: Unmasking AI
subtitle: My Mission to Protect What Is Human in a World of Machines
pitch: A computer scientist found face recognition could not see her dark skinned face until she wore a white mask. Her memoir follows the research and activism that followed.

chapters.g: As a graduate student at the MIT Media Lab, Buolamwini's face was not detected until she put on a white mask.
Her research audit found commercial face analysis was far less accurate for darker skinned women.
Her term for the priorities and prejudices of those who build technology, carried into the systems.
Testifying to lawmakers, poetry, and founding the Algorithmic Justice League.
People harmed by AI systems, and the fight for consent and redress.

ideas: AI systems can fail people unequally.
Audits can reveal and reduce bias.
The coded gaze reflects the builders' blind spots.
People deserve a say in how AI affects them.

args.a: Biased AI causes real harm and needs regulation.
args.c: Companies improved accuracy after audits, and some argue industry can fix bias itself.

args.a: Some uses, like police face recognition, should be limited.
args.c: Others argue face recognition helps solve crimes when used with care.

questions: Who is left out of the data your favourite AI was trained on?
Should face recognition be used by police?
What is one audit you would run on an AI tool?

quiz.q: What did Buolamwini wear to be detected?
quiz.w: The moment that started her work.

o: A study of bias in face analysis
